38	两台服务器（bjb1/westd）均搜索确认 seed1 (exp029_episode_level/global_step_15_hf) 和 seed3 (exp029_seed3_v2/global_step_15_hf) 的 HF 和 FSDP checkpoint 均不存在——已在之前磁盘清理中删除。Table 1 中 seed1 (23.88%) 和 seed3 (10.45%) 只能使用已有 OOD 结果。

40	## 决策原因
41	
42	### 8B Cell C 用 FSDP2 + CPUOffloadPolicy (2026-05-19)
43	FSDP1 峰值 ~91 GB/GPU → OOM（v5-v8 全部失败）。FSDP2 CPUOffloadPolicy 将参数和优化器按 layer 搬到 CPU，峰值降至 ~83 GB/GPU，余量 ~12 GB。不需要租卡。
44	
45	### ScienceWorld GRPO reward 是 continuous sparse (2026-05-19)
46	公式：`reward = (score/100) * 10.0`，范围 0-10，仅 episode 结束发放。Cell A（step-level）预期失败：中间步 reward=0，最后一步有 continuous reward 但 step-level credit assignment 无法利用。Cell C（episode-level）自然兼容。
47	
48	### 崩溃 seed OOD 泛化最强 — 关键 narrative 发现 (2026-05-21)
49	Seed 4（collapse seed, step 15）OOD = 30.60%，超过所有 success seeds（max 29.10%）。response_length inflation（7212 tokens）在 OOD 场景充当"暴力搜索"——更长的探索覆盖更多动作组合。崩溃不是纯粹有害的：训练集上是退化，OOD 上是更好的探索性。Bimodal behavior 是 "efficient learner vs over-explorer" 的权衡，不是简单的 "success vs failure"。
50	
51	### max_response_length 在 RAGEN 代码中无原生实现 (2026-05-21)
52	`config/base.yaml` 中 `data.max_response_length` 仅通过 OmegaConf 插值映射到 per-turn `rollout.response_length`，无 trajectory-level 截断逻辑。C' 实验在 bjb1 `agent_proxy.py` 中手动实现了 cumulative token 计数器（L253-339），此改动只在 bjb1 上，westd 代码未改。
53	
54	## 约束
55	
56	### westd GPU 内存紧张 (2026-05-19)
57	8B FSDP2+CPUOffload 训练时 GPU 占用 ~83/95.6 GB (87%)。不要增加 batch size 或 max_model_len，无余量。

Key differences: (a) planning is generative and open-ended, while verification is diagnostic and brief with behavioral output; (b) fixed cost penalty vs. our Lagrangian adaptive cost + behaviorally-grounded informativeness; (c) no informativeness analysis. TON: Think or Not (arXiv 2505.16854, NeurIPS 2025) uses GRPO for binary think/not-think decisions via two-stage training (SFT with thought dropout → GRPO exploration) in VLMs. Achieves up to 90% token reduction on reasoning benchmarks and is also evaluated on the AITZ agentic navigation task (3.6K→0.9K tokens). Key differences: (a) primarily single-turn VLM reasoning and basic agentic navigation, not multi-turn interactive agents with irreversible environmental actions and sparse rewards; (b) task-accuracy reward only, no behavioral grounding or informativeness signal; (c) thought dropout SFT warm-start vs. our always-on verification capability warm-start from Self-Guide. The two-stage GRPO approach is methodological precedent for our Component 1→2 transition. Thinkless (arXiv 2505.13379, NeurIPS 2025) introduces DeGRPO (Decoupled GRPO) for binary <short>/<think> control tokens in LLMs. Achieves 50-90% reduction in long-chain thinking on math reasoning. Complementary to TON; differs from our work in the same ways (single-turn, no behavioral grounding). AVA: Anytime Verified Agents (OpenReview JMDCMf7mlF, TMLR 2026) dynamically allocates compute across search, sampling, and selective verification cascades under budget constraints using calibrated uncertainty estimation and value-of-information-guided search expansion with early exits. Evaluated on GSM8K, MATH, HotpotQA, HumanEval with API models (GPT-5, GPT-4o). Key differences: (a) inference-time uncertainty-based heuristic allocation, not RL-trained verification selectivity; (b) operates on single-turn reasoning tasks, not interactive multi-step agents; (c) relies on calibrated uncertainty rather than behavioral-change signals; (d) uses API models without fine-tuning. AVA addresses 'when to verify under budget constraints' at inference time; we train the selectivity into the model via RL with behavioral grounding. AdaCoT (arXiv 2505.11896, May 2025) frames when-to-reason as Pareto optimization via PPO with adaptive penalty, achieving 69% token reduction. Key differences: (a) single-turn reasoning, not interactive agents with irreversible actions; (b) CoT is continuous-length, verification is discrete binary with behavioral signal; (c) no informativeness reward. BATS (arXiv 2511.17006, Nov 2025) provides systematic study on budget-constrained agents using heuristic strategy adaptation. Key differences: (a) plug-in heuristic, not RL-trained; (b) tool-call budget, not step-level self-verification; (c) no verification quality analysis. RISE (arXiv 2505.13445, NeurIPS 2025) simultaneously trains problem-solving and self-verification via RL with verifiable rewards, showing self-verification behaviors emerge during reasoning. Key differences: (a) single-turn mathematical reasoning, not multi-turn interactive agents with irreversible environmental actions; (b) verification integrated into reasoning chain, not a discrete binary decision per step; (c) no selectivity mechanism or cost-quality tradeoff analysis. Uno-Orchestra (arXiv 2605.05007, May 2026) jointly optimizes task decomposition and worker selection via RL on multi-agent orchestration, achieving 77.0% macro pass@1 across 13 benchmarks at 10× lower cost. Key differences: (a) routing/delegation across models, not intra-agent self-verification; (b) optimizes worker selection, not verification timing; (c) no self-check informativeness signal. CoVe (arXiv 2603.01940, March 2026) trains interactive tool-use agents via constraint-guided verification on τ²-bench, achieving 43-59% pass@1 competitive with 17× larger models. Key differences: (a) uses external deterministic constraint verifiers, not learned self-verification; (b) verification quality defined by constraint satisfaction, not behavioral correction; (c) does not learn WHEN to verify — constraints are always applied during training. ReVeal (arXiv 2506.11442) introduces TAPO (Turn-Aware Policy Optimization) for code agents, preventing reward gaming via turn-level credit assignment. Relevant methodology: our B-IAVR's behavioral grounding similarly prevents gaming by tying rewards to action changes rather than self-check labels. iStar (arXiv 2509.19199) combines implicit step rewards with episode-level advantages for agent RL credit assignment on WebShop, achieving efficient exploration. Relevant to our step-vs-episode reward design. GiGPO (arXiv 2505.10978, NeurIPS 2025) introduces two-level grouping (episode + step) for fine-grained credit assignment in verl-agent, achieving >12% gains on ALFWorld and >9% on WebShop over GRPO. Complementary to our approach — we use GRPO for consistency with Self-Guide baselines, but GiGPO integration is natural future work. Leash (arXiv 2512.21540, Dec 2025) uses Lagrangian primal-dual adaptive penalty to reduce reasoning length by 60%; we adopt this for verification budget control. SelfBudgeter (arXiv 2505.11274) trains two-phase GRPO for token budget estimation; latest arXiv revision (v6, April 2026) remains under review. AutoThink (arXiv 2505.10832, NeurIPS 2025) learns reasoning mode switching via multi-stage RL. Self-Verification Dilemma (arXiv 2602.03485, Feb 2026) identifies confirmatory over-verification; our B-IAVR operationalizes this insight via behavioral grounding. Agentic Critical Training (arXiv 2603.08706, March 2026) trains self-reflection via RL without cost modeling. LLMs Gaming Verifiers (arXiv 2604.15149, April 2026) demonstrates that RLVR-trained models can exploit verification signals for reward hacking, validating our concern about category-based IAVR and motivating the behavioral grounding in B-IAVR. KEY POSITIONING: The GRPO-based selective compute family (TON, Thinkless, AdaCoT) provides strong methodological precedent for learning binary compute-allocation decisions, but operates in single-turn settings without behavioral grounding. AVA provides the closest 'when to verify under budget' framing but uses inference-time heuristics rather than RL-trained selectivity. Unlike all prior work on selective compute allocation and concurrent work on agent verification, B-IAVR introduces a behaviorally-grounded training objective that rewards verification only when it changes the agent's action — exploiting the unique causal structure of self-guidance in interactive environments where actions have observable consequences.
